title: The square-zero difference coordinate of a group space is additive
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with identity $e:S\to G$, multiplication $m:G\times_SG\to G$ and inverse satisfying the group identities; commutativity and smoothness are not assumed. Let $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], defined by an ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$, so $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Write $G(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,G)$ with the product $xy=m\circ(x,y)$, $e_T$ for its identity, $e_0:T_0\to S\xrightarrow{e}G$, and $K=\ker(G(T)\to G(T_0))$. On the small etale site of $T_0$, identified with that of $T$ along $j$, let $\widetilde I$ be the module sheaf associated to the $A/I$-module $I$, and let $\Omega^1_{G/S}$ be the module of relative differentials on the small etale site of $G$, representing $S$-derivations of its structure sheaf into module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; $e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S}=\mathcal O_{T_0}\otimes_{e_0^{-1}\mathcal O_G}e_0^{-1}\Omega^1_{G/S}$. For $b\in K$ the difference $b^\sharp-e_T^\sharp:e_0^{-1}\mathcal O_G\to\widetilde I$ of the two ring-sheaf maps is an $S$-derivation; let $\delta(b)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\widetilde I)$ be the corresponding homomorphism. Then $\delta(e_T)=0$ and $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)+\delta(y)$ for all $x,y\in K$.

proof.text: Put $M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\widetilde I)$. The $A$-action on $I$ factors through $A/I$, since $I^2=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] to $X=G$, $a=e_T$, and the given thickening, whose ideal sheaf is $\widetilde I$. Its lift set $L_G(e_0)$ is exactly $K$. The resulting pointed bijection $\delta_G:K\to M$ is the map $\delta$ of the statement: both are represented by $b^\sharp-e_T^\sharp$. In particular this difference is an $S$-derivation and $\delta(e_T)=0$. No smoothness or presentation hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening; agent application of their linearization to group multiplication.

proof.text: Let $P=G\times_SG$, $a_P=(e_T,e_T)$, and $p_0=(e_0,e_0)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] to obtain $\delta_P:L_P(p_0)\to M_P$, where $M_P=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(p_0^*\Omega^1_{P/S},\widetilde I)$. Its naturality clause gives linear maps $q_i=(\operatorname{pr}_i)_*:M_P\to M$. The linear map $q=(q_1,q_2):M_P\to M\times M$ is bijective: under $\delta_P$ and $\delta_G$ it is the map taking a lift to its two components, whose inverse pairs any two lifts in $K$. Its inverse is additive, since applying injective $q$ to $q^{-1}(v+w)$ and $q^{-1}(v)+q^{-1}(w)$ gives $v+w$ in both cases; the identical argument proves scalar compatibility.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening; agent application of their linearization to group multiplication.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] for $u=m:P\to G$, postcomposition induces a linear map $m_*:M_P\to M$, because $ma_P=e_T$. Define the linear map $F=m_*q^{-1}:M\times M\to M$. Naturality and the definition of $q$ give $\delta(xy)=F(\delta(x),\delta(y))$. For $v\in M$, choose $x=\delta_G^{-1}(v)$; the unit identities $xe_T=x=e_Tx$ give $F(v,0)=v=F(0,v)$. Therefore $F(v,w)=F((v,0)+(0,w))=v+w$. This proves $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)+\delta(y)$ for all $x,y\in K$. The argument only uses linearity and the two unit identities, so it applies without commutativity of $G$.
